_about: What llms.txt and llms-full.txt say about the site: the intro paragraph, one line and a name for each page (in the order they are listed), and quick facts. Written by hand (research, 2026-09-30); design/check-site.mjs checks that every page has a line.
intro: Lucida is a flashcard app that runs in the browser at app.lucida.cards, on phones, tablets and computers. It plans every review with FSRS spaced repetition, and your own AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any app that supports MCP) can make and edit your cards through a personal link, so studying itself doesn’t need an AI subscription. Cards can be question and answer, fill in the blank, a picture with hidden parts (image occlusion) or sound, and Learn mode quizzes you on them. The free plan has unlimited decks and cards, FSRS reviews, Learn mode, shared decks, classes, live games with friends, up to 100 pictures and sounds, and import and export. Pro costs $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year and adds exam dates, weak-spot stats, unlimited pictures and sounds, themes and more. There is no App Store app yet. Support: team@lucida.cards.

facts: Runs in the browser at app.lucida.cards on any device. The native iPhone app isn’t on the App Store yet. It needs an internet connection.
Sign in with an email code, Google or Apple. You must be 13 or older.
Scheduling is FSRS version 5 (19 parameters). Default remember goal 90% (70 to 97% per deck), 20 new cards a day, no daily review limit.
Card kinds: question and answer, fill in the blank, picture (image occlusion, up to 30 boxes a picture) and sound.
Your AI connects through a personal MCP link and can add up to 500 cards per request. It is free on the free plan.
Free: unlimited decks and cards, FSRS, Learn mode, shared decks, classes, live games (up to 60 players, no account to join), up to 100 pictures and sounds, import and export.

Pro: $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year. Adds exam dates, weak-spot stats, unlimited pictures and sounds, themes, hardest cards on decks you share, photo covers, natural voices for sound cards, more AI explanations, and tuning to your own reviews.
Import: Anki’s Notes in Plain Text export, Quizlet’s Export, CSV, TSV and pasted text. Not .apkg files. Imported cards start as new cards.
Export: one deck as CSV, or everything (decks, cards and review history) as lucida.json.
Privacy: no ads, no selling data, and cards aren’t used to train AI models, per the privacy policy.
